newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - March 7.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - March 7.

text.p: THE AUSTRALIAN

Warren Lockwood was elected unopposed as chairman of the New South Wales Rugby league board yesterday, immediately easing concerns that clubs may have to merge if Melbourne was brought into the current competition. He admitted that the issue might have to be addressed in the future. Page 36.

Fighting a degenerative knee disorder which may threaten his career, Australian footballer Ben Allan yesterday stepped down as captain of the Perth club. Allan resigned the captaincy after it was determined that his knee will not allow him to play as much as he would have liked. Page 36.

Sydney United goalkeeper Zeljko Kalac confirmed yesterday that he will play with English first division soccer side Portsmouth. Australian Socceroos boss Terry Venables is chairman and majority (51 per cent) owner of the Portsmouth club. Page 35.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Women look set to enter another arena of the Australian Jockey Club. Three women have made it onto the short-list of eight for cadet stewards. If successful the women will be the first female stewards in the history of New South Wales' horseracing. Page 39.

There is growing speculation that the Canberra Cosmos soccer club will be one of the first clubs to be cut from the league. Despite finishing the season with a history of poor crowds and recurring financial problems, chairman Paul Murphy says the club is set to make significant improvements and progress starting from next season. Page 38.

Australian cycling coach Charlie Walsh was yesterday confirmed as a co-selector of national track teams. Walsh's selection has come just a week before the Australian championships in Launceston. Page 40.
THE AGE

Newly appointed Australian Football League commissioner David Shaw last night admitted that the Carlton football club has breached its salary cap by several hundred thousand dollars. Shaw said he had seen documents which confirmed that Carlton was one of a number of such clubs. Page 8.

Australian pole vaulter Emma George was among sporting elites such as Moses Kipketer and Michael Johnston yesterday when she attended a media conference on the eve of the world indoor athletics championships in Paris. Since breaking her first world record little more than a year ago, George has become hot property - setting records almost every time she competes. Page 8.

Australian paceman Paul Reiffel returns to the Australian cricket side after being out with a hamstring injury. Reiffel will join the Australians to take on Border in the first-class match in East London tomorrow. However Reiffel will need a brilliant prformance to convince selectors to change the bowling line-up that slaughtered South Africa in the First Test. Page 6.
THE HERALD SUN

Ferrari's $30 million man, Michael Schumacher says he cannot win the Australian Grand Prix on Sunday. The early verdict has been backed by Ferrari team manager Jean Todt, although both concede luck could play an important part. Page 110.

Melbourne company The Breakaway Group has unveiled ambitious plans to turn Waverly Park into the world's first sporting theme park. Preliminary plans estimate the cost of such a revamp at $200 million, in a move which would see Waverly retained as a footall stadium. Page 108.

Champion Australian horse trainer Bart Cummings was last night named Victorian Racing trainer of the year for the third time. Last year Cummings won the Melbourne Cup for a record tenth time with Saintly. Page 108.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Five clubs have made offers to banned super league player Jack Elsegood for the 1997 season - each offering the minimum loyalty guarantee of $150,000 for the season. St George, Sydney City, Newcastle, Balmain and South Sydney have all made offers to the star winger. Page 120.

Coached by former Australian cricket captain Allan Border, the Australian youth cricket team has thrashed the Pakistan youth XI by 145 runs in a three-day match. Australia declared at 3-318 on day one of a three-day game and then rolled the home team for 160. Page 117.

Several Super League clubs have been angered by a decision to ban the use of revolutionary new leather gloves to improve handling. Super League official have said they need time to fully examine the glove issue. Page 112.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
